lines.en: From that point on, everything is surreal.
Which isn’t to say it wasn’t already. But the fact that these things that once would have terrified me are now being treated so nonchalantly is...
Well, I don’t really know how to feel.
And I’m trying not to feel much of anything at all for Himawari’s sake since I know she’s working hard right now.
We move from place to place and girl to girl.
I watch as she rests her hand on each of their heads and rearranges their memories like it’s no more difficult than folding clothes.
And then they just lie there. Dormant. Unconsciously waiting for all of this to blow over when they’ll be picked up like pieces on a chess board and placed wherever it is they’re meant to be.
Then a new game will begin. And I will be the one to make the first move because this world apparently won’t turn at all if I am not the one to start spinning it.
At first, each body is a lot like Sana’s. Limp and slumped over at an awkward angle — sometimes propped up against something — but, other times, it’s different.
Sometimes, it looks like there was a moment of sentience that somehow penetrated the barrier between where we were and where we are now.
Yasu’s body was covered in scratches.
Miku had pulled some of her hair out again. I can’t remember the last time she did that.
And then there was Noriko — who’d spent her final moments digging for something so frantically that I thought I caught a glimpse of bone in her fingers before Himawari asked me to look away.
I feel like I could have looked without consequence, though. For this is all too unexpectedly nostalgic for me to let any pain in.
It reminds me of when I broke through the past on the way to a false future and wound up here of all places — an intermission.
Or maybe even the type of loading screen you’d get when restarting your favorite game just to find out that the script changed itself and some of your progress carried over.
I wonder, if I could read my story again with the knowledge I have now, just how much would change. But I’m not sure I ever will, and that’s not purely because I don’t have the time to.
It’s because I am afraid of how I’d see my past self when, for the first time in my life, I am confident that I am doing something right.
I watch as Himawari emerges from the room in which we held our traditional “end of the world” party this time. She wouldn’t let me inside.
There’s no curiosity on my end once she’s back in the hall, though. It’s just pride — something I don’t often feel in the ways I should.
And when I look at her, clearly unperturbed by the horrors she has faced, all I can think of is how strong she is.
And how I am so eternally grateful that she did not grow up to be like me.
: Okay. So, barring Mom and the girls outside of your class that Shiori is currently hunting for, we’re still missing: Ami, Futaba, Nodoka, and Rin.
: Where did you get a clipboard from? Why aren’t you just using your phone like a normal girl?
: This feels more official, obviously. Using my phone would just make it look like I’m texting somebody and I don’t want you thinking I’m irresponsible enough to do that at work.
: You’ve done plenty today to make me think you’re irresponsible at work. But, despite you breaking so many rules, I do know you’re doing it for me. So I’m very thankful, Himawari.
: Well, don’t thank me just yet. We still need to find these stragglers.
: After that, maybe we can stop for lunch somewhere and you can tell me again how awesome I am.
: Does your app thing not tell you where they are? I figured you could just...press a button and get their coordinates or something.
: Or am I the only one you have direct surveillance over?
: I can get the last known location of everyone. But once the clock stops, tracking doesn’t work anymore.
: So any movement that occurs subsequent to the events of what you call the “apocalypse” doesn’t register. Which means anyone who moved needs to be tracked down.
: Normally, this wouldn’t be much of an issue as we’re free to pause and un-pause time as we see fit. But I’m not the one maintaining time here at the moment, so-
: Wait, hold on. Are you saying that all of the girls you just mentioned kept moving around after time stopped? Like what we’re doing now?
: That’s right. That shouldn’t come as that much of a surprise though when you’ve already seen Mom, Maya, and Makoto do it.
: Yeah, notice how none of the girls you’re looking for are on that list? They shouldn’t be able to move at all right now. They should have disappeared.
: Oh. Yeah, nobody really disappears. You just stop seeing them. Like what happened with Maya that one time when you woke up and she was all like “Aaaaaah” and then Mom was like “Woaaaaah.”
: This could be huge, then. Because I can see everyone just fine when you’re here. And if the number of girls who make it to the roof is still expanding, we might be onto something.
: Maybe. But just because they managed to move around after the clock stopped doesn’t mean they’re still moving now. So please don’t get your hopes up.
: I hope you mean that they’re just sitting around waiting and not the other thing that could mean.
: It could mean a bunch of things. Waiting. Suicide. Divine interference. Even that someone else moved them. Though, I’m not really sure who would in this case unless Mom is actually evil.
: Oh my god. Imagine she was? And that the only reason she didn’t come with us on our excursion is so she could go sabotage the clean-up crew?
: I mean...not to add to your conspiracy theory, but she does have a history of custodial murder.
: Then time is even more pressing, Dad. You don’t have any idea where any of those girls would be, do you?
: If Ami and Nodoka aren’t here, I don’t really know where they would be. But Rin and Futaba went back to the dorms from what I understand.
: Did they? Then why are they still marked off as being at the inn?
: I...don’t know. I remember them leaving, though. Right after Futaba went on a massive, uncharacteristic tirade about the nature of the world and how much of a douchebag I am.
: And you didn’t think that “massive uncharacteristic tirade about the nature of the world” was something worth mentioning? Just gonna keep that info in your back pocket?
: You could at least get mad about her calling me a douchebag.
: I’m about to call you a douchebag too for concealing relevant information from a divine official. I hope you have a lawyer ready.
: I have two now, actually. I’ll see you in court.
: Sorry — trial’s in recess.
: But it hasn’t even started yet.
: Come on. Take my hand again. We’ll go check the dorms and see if they’re still around. After that, though, we need to make finding Ami a priority. She can be a troublesome one.
: What? What is that supposed to-
: I’d rather you find out from her and not me. But that’s info for later. Come, Father. Hold your daughter’s hand in this dark and scary world. She requires your protection.
: Okay...But if I don’t find out from her-
: Don’t worry. I’ll tell you myself if I have to. I promise I won’t leave until you know.
: I wish you’d just promise to not leave at all.
: So do I. And one day, I will.
: But for now...
: Our scavenger hunt continues!
: I hope you’re ready to find even more body parts this time. Horseface Taki’s Power Hour continues now.
: Have you actually met him or is he just a thing I made up that you know about for some reason?
: He’s real. Just a lesser god though. Doesn’t even show up on the popularity polls.
: You have popularity polls?
: Oh, totally. It’s a great way to farm engagement and acquire new customers. You’ll see ads for them on TV and everything if we ever get you out of here.
: I’m not sure I want to leave anymore. I don’t even like seeing them in my dreams. I don’t need them infiltrating reality.
: I mean, technically speaking, it’s us who infiltrated reality. Most of the gods predate us by, like...zillions of years. In the context of this world, though, I get what you’re saying.
: It’s probably not as bad as you think, though. With so many gods offering different things for different individuals, it gives almost everyone something to believe in.
: And having them work alongside humans did a lot to build trust between them and the people. So it’s not really anything like the way it is here.
: So they’re not only reaching out to people for their own benefit now?
: They are. They need to in order to keep existing. But it’s a mostly symbiotic relationship that emphasizes mutual benefit rather than just one party’s gain.
: There will always be bad actors, of course. Some gods still act more like snake-oil salesmen than divine figures.
: But the world has caught on and they’re the ones fizzling out now. Especially since most of them lack professional representation.
: Can’t help but feel bad for all the atheists out there, though. Like, damn. Egg on your face. They’re basically just the new version of flat-earthers.
: I honestly can’t tell if any of this is legitimate or if it’s just another mahjong situation.
: Believe whatever you want to believe. That’s the prevailing and accepted stance now. But, if it’s cool, I have a question for you, Dad.
: Me? Sure. What is it?
: Isn’t there supposed to be more “dorm” there?
: There probably should be, yeah.
: How do you even get up here without teleportation?
: There’s a lot about this building that doesn’t make any sense. We’ve all just sort of tuned it out, I think.
: Sure. But really, though. How the hell do you get up here?
: You’re the one with a live-feed of my existence. Just tune in one day and find out for yourself.
: I think I’d rather just not know than remove the dorms from my blacklist. I know what goes on here.
: On that note, you are forbidden from ever staying in any dorm. I want you to remember that even if I don’t wind up escaping.
: That’s fine. It’d be harder recording all of my ASMR videos with a roommate anyway.
: You will escape, though. And I don’t want you to even acknowledge the possibility of that not happening.
: You’re putting a lot of faith in me, Himawari. I needed to have my hand held both literally and figuratively to find out literally any of this.
: Maya didn’t know either and she did this for thousands if not millions of years. How can I find a way out if I don’t even know where I am? Or what else exists?
: You know I exist.
: And if I found you, I know you can find me too.
: You have a clear advantage as a time and dimension-hopping divine custodian. I’m little more than a clone of my imaginary girlfriend’s desires.
: You’re no clone, Dad. You’re the real thing. You were just dragged somewhere you were never meant to be, and now we’re going to take you home.
: But, in order to do that, we must first find the rest of your harem! Futaba and Rin are in Dorm 4, right?
: Right. But, if Rin is in there, don’t make eye contact with her. I don’t want her falling in love with you.
: I’ll take one for the team if it means giving Mom an advantage. Maybe Futaba will fall in love with me too and I’ll have knocked two competitors off the list at once?
: Or they’re just not in there and none of this will matter.
: Only one way to find out, I guess. Please hold while I investigate.
: Yeah. Doesn’t look like they’re here.
: Really? Maybe the coffee shop Rin works at then? I can see her going there in the event of an apocalypse.
: I’ll just ask Shi-chan to keep an eye out for them so we can get to looking for Ami.
: Her dorm is just across the hall. I doubt she’s in there, though. I imagine she would have come out the second she heard my voice if she was.
: Want to check yourself while I make a quick phone call?
: Hm? Yeah, I can do that. It’ll also give me time to warn her that you aren’t a threat. That’s a thing I need to do with her now.
: Works for me! Be right back! And don’t fall off the ledge!
: Oh, that reminds me. There’s another ledge I found with Io that-
: Hold that thought! Phone is ringing!
